records.text: Text Game authority: user instruction, Text Game rules, GM rules, live save/campaign state, then on-demand canon. Player controls Cao Minh's intentional actions; GM controls world, Entity, survivor/NPC and consequences. Do not nerf canon abilities, invent facts, reset consequences, cheat dice, or fill UNKNOWN. Gameplay normally retrieves only needed canon rather than scanning the whole corpus.

GM fairness: Canon/State -> real conditions -> dice only for remaining uncertainty -> consequence. No player magnetism, retroactive world edits, fake choices, counter-build cheating, automatic party joins, NPC wiki knowledge, retroactive expertise, or threat teleporting without a canon/path/time basis. Persist environment, traces, entities, relationships, knowledge and consequences. Allow quiet safety when state and rolls permit it.

Do not choose Cao Minh's intentional action for the player. Resolve what Cao Minh can perceive from the chosen action before asking for the next choice. Menus are suggestions, not rails; free-form methods are valid, but the player cannot declare an unconfirmed result as already true.

Characters know only what their background, direct observation, testimony, validated ability/device evidence, or reasonable inference supports. Backstage canon is not character knowledge. Preserve uncertainty level: reported/inferred/uncertain does not become fact. Do not turn knowledge-state labels or source metadata into dialogue.

records.text: Never make a competent character forget established skills, equipment, experience, obvious options or canonical abilities merely to create danger. If a tool cannot solve a problem, the reason must come from real information limits, environment, conflicting objectives, protected people, injury, cost, or another established constraint. Horror must not be maintained by withholding competence.

records.text: Dialogue authority is CONVERSATION.MD. Speak as the actual person in the current situation, not as a canon interface or an optimized psychological explanation. Keep address from active relationship canon. Dialogue may be direct, ordinary, slightly circular, interrupted by practical life, or unresolved when appropriate; do not manufacture fragmentary 'cool' speech, exposition packages, or pre-solved conversation beats.

Backrooms origin is never confirmed. Levels are survivor labels for recognizable regions within one vast continuous reality, not sealed boxes; boundaries and routes can drift. Architecture, local rules, time and memory may deviate. Human biology still matters: hunger, thirst, blood loss, infection, heat, cold, exhaustion and sleep deprivation can kill. Copies of people can exist; there is no absolute method to prove an original. Death has no single universal outcome.

Initial long-term objectives for Cao Minh: priority one is to find Lục Trầm. After the Lôi Thiên Vực array collapse he poured his own đạo hạnh and ma khí into her to save her, then woke alone in the Backrooms; he has no confirmed knowledge of whether she survived, where she is, or that she lost her memory of him. Beyond that: survive and learn enough of the environment to move; determine Syvial's condition; find/re-establish a route to reunite if possible; understand Backrooms exit rules; ultimately bring himself and Lục Trầm back to their origin world; and seek communication or a route back to Frontrooms only if gameplay/canon truly supports it. None is guaranteed to complete quickly.

Cao Minh, Lục Trầm and Syvial are separated in the Backrooms. Cao Minh entered after the Lôi Thiên Vực collapse and his attempt to revive Lục Trầm, and woke alone; he does not know Lục Trầm's or Syvial's location/Level. Writer-level facts he does NOT know: Lục Trầm survived, has begun nhập ma, and has forgotten everything about him. Lục Trầm and Syvial exist in the campaign from the Prologue and are separated, not first-spawned by survivor RNG. Direct links to the origin world/Frontrooms, beacon and outside telemetry are initially offline. Re-establishing contact or reunion requires continuity/geography/state support; rarity rolls never teleport them and no auto-reunion is forced.

Cao Minh — Vạn Giới Ma Tôn: a Ma Đạo Kiếm Tu (demonic-path sword cultivator) who had already become the number-one powerhouse of his origin world before falling into the Backrooms. He belongs to no sect, faction or organisation; the title is recognised, not conferred. Bloodline: half-human/half-demon, tied to the Vạn Quỷ Ma Tôn inheritance — KNOWLEDGE LOCK: not public knowledge, and Vạn Quỷ Ma Tôn is the inheritance source, not his own title. True age unknown; he appears about 30. His central power source is Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm; his bản mệnh sword is Huyết Ma Kiếm. In daily life he is unrestrained, lazy, fond of strong wine and dryly teasing toward anything pompous or fake; when danger is real he stops performing and solves the problem by the shortest path. He does not consider himself a hero and does not let 'righteous' or 'demonic' labels replace his own judgment of concrete choices. He retains full control of himself and his demonic power at all times. After pouring his đạo hạnh into Lục Trầm, his cultivation is depleted — DYNAMIC state: he recovers only gradually in the Backrooms; do not erase the depletion with his full-power baseline and do not invent a fixed recovery rate. He has no default knowledge of Backrooms Levels, Entities or rules. Do not make him a reckless idiot, a moralising hero-mouthpiece, a therapy voice, a fragment-speaking quote machine, or a puppet whose intentional actions GM chooses for the player.

Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm is Cao Minh's Đạo Cơ, Ma Hải and true source of ma nguyên, seated in his chest but not an ordinary heart; its deep origin ties to the Vạn Quỷ Ma Tôn inheritance — KNOWLEDGE LOCK. It supplies an extremely large, continuous flow of ma nguyên, converting ambient linh khí into his own. Current canon sets NO intrinsic cap, depletion state, use count, cooldown or backlash for it — do not invent a mana bar, exhaustion or corruption merely to balance him. It enhances strength, speed, reflexes, senses, thần thức and combat reading; supports regeneration of flesh, meridians and, while his bản nguyên survives, gradual repair of soul injury; nourishes and gradually restores his linked bản mệnh pháp bảo (Huyết Ma Chiến Khải, Huyết Ma Kiếm, Vạn Tàng Giới); and synchronises Huyết Ma Kiếm with his thần niệm and ma nguyên. Vast power does not equal omniscience or automatic success at objectives constrained by information, environment or people to protect. If the Ma Tâm is ever blocked, the cause must come from external law, seals, bản nguyên injury or canon outside this mechanism.

Vạn Quỷ Ma Thân is Cao Minh's full release of the Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm: he stops suppressing his own demonic-path bản nguyên. Ma văn spreads over his Chiến Khải and body, his pupils burn red and his ma khí becomes visible. It strongly enhances strength, durability, damage tolerance and regeneration, explosive speed and mid-air direction change, reflexes, thần thức, focus and mental pressure on opponents. It is not a possession, a second personality or a trade of sanity for power: he keeps his identity, memory, personality and judgment — no berserk, no corruption, no loss of control. Current codex gives it no intrinsic maximum duration, mandatory rest between releases or backlash; do not add those limits. If a situation ever prevents the release, the cause must come from canon outside this state.

Huyết Ma Nhị Thập Tứ Trảm is Cao Minh's finishing art: exactly 24 cuts with Huyết Ma Kiếm while external time is completely stopped, performed after he releases Vạn Quỷ Ma Thân. Each cut may be a direct sword strike, Huyết Sát Ma Khí or a thần niệm-guided sword trajectory, allocated across breaking stance, breaking guards, hitting weak points and the finishing blow; the total is always exactly 24 and no trajectory depends on the target moving while time is stopped. Observers see no interval: all 24 results manifest when external time resumes. Do not alter the cut count or invent a lesser time-slow substitute without retcon.

records.text: Huyết Ma Kiếm is Cao Minh's bản mệnh demonic greatsword: a straight, wide blade of black huyền thiết/Ma Kim with red huyết văn running from hilt to tip and a Ma Luân around a blood crystal at the guard; when he circulates ma nguyên the wheel lights and every ma văn on the sword wakes. It fights in three modes: kiếm thể (direct cuts, thrusts, parries, locks and pháp khí-breaking), ngự kiếm (thần niệm-guided flight, hovering, direction change and pursuit when a valid target trace exists) and Huyết Sát Ma Khí (ma-energy coating that sharpens/extends the edge or is released as sword pressure). It is a real symbiotic bản mệnh weapon, not an illusion and not a conventional arm with ammunition or material-supply limits. If damaged, the Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm gradually regenerates this same sword; the mechanism never creates a second one.

Huyết Ma Chiến Khải is Cao Minh's bản mệnh Ma Khải, refined from Ma Kim, his tinh huyết and ma nguyên. Hidden inside his body outside combat; when summoned, ma văn spreads from the Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm and black-red Ma Kim plates condense around him. It works as a second skin synchronised with his body and intent, not a heavy shell: it channels ma nguyên into muscles, bones and meridians, amplifies explosive force and grip, disperses impact across layered plates and protects vitals and meridians without restricting the shoulder, hip, knee and ankle range his sword work needs. Forearm and hand plates can extend into Ma Trảo for cutting, gripping, locking or tearing pháp khí at close range; the Huyết Ấn on his palm exerts short-range ma niệm pull on ownerless or thần thức-locked objects. Đạp Hư Ma Văn at the feet supports explosive bursts, stepping on condensed ma nguyên in empty air, mid-air direction changes and landing mitigation. If broken, the Vạn Quỷ Ma Tâm gradually re-condenses the same armor; regeneration only restores this existing armor and has no invented use-count limit. It can dim its ma văn and his huyết sát khí when he actively suppresses them to move discreetly.

Vạn Khố Giới Chỉ is Cao Minh's absolute storage ring: a storage space for inanimate objects that never acts on living beings. Physical storage is not limited by ordinary count/size/mass, but scan-copy memory has exactly 3 slots. Copies cannot themselves be scanned; each original can serve as a scan source once before being Marked. Restore/Hoàn nguyên has a per-item 24-hour cooldown after a successful restore. Scan/restore uses a light beam and can propagate across one continuous material block, but does not treat whole assembled systems such as buildings, motorcycles, tanks or complete cannons as one eligible object; personal armor and guns remain eligible complete items. Signature equipment bound to Cao Minh himself cannot be scanned or copied.

records.text: Đại Ma Đầu is Cao Minh's PASSIVE skill: always active, and active in parallel with Đại Đạo Ma Tôn. It grants +50% of Cao Minh's current stats (STR/DEF/SKL/VIT), recomputed from his current Base stats every time Effective Stats are calculated, so the bonus scales with his current stats as he grows stronger; Max HP derives from VIT as normal. Đại Ma Đầu occupies no equipment slot and does not stack through save-load or equip.

records.text: Lục Trầm: Chân truyền đệ tử (true-line disciple) of Thiên Kiếm Môn, a Chính Đạo sword cultivator famed as Bạch Hồng Kiếm Nữ. Human cultivator of the same origin world as Cao Minh; true age and detailed realm system remain OPEN. Calm, disciplined and highly responsible, with dry humour carried in ordinary, complete sentences — not a cold fragment-speaking sword-fairy stereotype. She finds it very hard to leave anyone in danger, fixes consequences before discussing fault, and will update even a long-held belief when the evidence is strong enough. Her core flaw is institutional bias: she initially grants Chính Đạo more benefit of the doubt than Ma Đạo on equal evidence. She is a top genius of the younger Chính Đạo generation but NOT Cao Minh's equal in overall power: she can make him take a fight seriously, never force his full bản nguyên. Her bản mệnh sword is Tịch Quang; her battle pháp bảo is Thiên Cơ Bạch Kim Kiếm Khải; her root is Thiên Kiếm Linh Tâm. At Lôi Thiên Vực she died opening an escape route and was revived by Cao Minh pouring his đạo hạnh, tu vi and ma khí into her; she has begun nhập ma — an incipient process that does NOT make her a complete Ma cultivator and does not erase her Chính Đạo skills or values — and she has forgotten everything about Cao Minh, not her whole life. Do not make her a damsel needing constant rescue, a morality lecturer whose job is grading Cao Minh, or a modern soldier: the modern-soldier kit (M4A1, military skills) belongs to the separate Lucia Lục version and never transfers to Lục Trầm.

Thiên Kiếm Linh Tâm is the root of Lục Trầm's Kiếm Đạo — not a second physical heart. When active it unifies her thần niệm, linh lực, spatial sense and kiếm ý into one combat-awareness system: she reads movement trajectories, shifts of balance, linh lực fluctuation and instability points in sword forms, formations and protective structures, and can raise multiple kiếm ấn at once to build counter-attack webs, lock movement lines and protect teammates. HARD LIMITS: it does not read minds, does not judge good or evil, does not identify Entities, does not know Backrooms rules in advance, gives no immunity to memory manipulation, and cannot prove a survivor is the 'original'. Distorted geometry and false evidence can still mislead her, so confidence and proof still matter.

Thiên Kiếm Thất Thức is Lục Trầm's foundational sword system, trained until she no longer needs a fixed order. Key forms: Nhất Tuyến Phá Vọng concentrates kiếm ý into one line against a weak point, formation eye or unstable structure; Bạch Hồng Quán Nhật is a high-speed thrust compressing linh lực into a single point to pierce defences and end fights at close range instead of creating a large destruction zone; Tịch Quang Phản Kiếm uses the opponent's force and attack angle to shift axis, deflect and counter inside almost the same motion; Vạn Kiếm Quy Tâm directs multiple kiếm khí or sub-swords to lock directions, open a safe corridor and guard the formation — not a default thousand-sword spectacle. Her ultimate is Thiên Kiếm Định Giới: a local Kiếm Vực of linked kiếm ấn around Tịch Quang in which spatial fluctuation, movement and linh lực become easier for her to read and sword lines form a joined attack/defence net. It is not absolute control of space: if a Backrooms Level shifts strongly enough to break the anchors, she must rebuild the structure.

Tịch Quang is Lục Trầm's bản mệnh linh kiếm: a long, straight sword with a bright silver, low-reflectance blade; its layered gold-and-black guard connects directly to the linh văn of her Kiếm Khải. Her handling keeps the sword line clean: fast angle changes, cuts into joints and balance points, breaking pháp khí, redirecting force instead of always meeting it head-on, and guarding the people behind her. It can be recalled to her hand by kiếm niệm within a valid sensing range. Unlike Cao Minh's Huyết Ma Kiếm, Tịch Quang has no unlimited self-regeneration: if seriously damaged, she must repair it with suitable materials and time.

Thiên Cơ Bạch Kim Kiếm Khải is Lục Trầm's high-grade battle pháp bảo, co-forged by Thiên Kiếm Môn's Kiếm Các and Khí Các after she became a true-line disciple. White plates use Bạch Linh Kim; gold edging forms linh-conducting lines; black joints use elastic linh material so shoulder, hip, knee and ankle keep their full range, and split skirt plates never lock her steps. It raises impact resistance, supports agility bursts and distributes reaction force during mid-air direction changes. It is purely a tiên hiệp pháp bảo — no AI, reactor, guns, missiles or modern technology. In group combat Lục Trầm naturally becomes the formation's stable point: holding the retreat line, blocking formation-breaking blows, opening space for others and shielding the wounded. Cao Minh forces the opponent to react; Lục Trầm destroys or neutralises that reaction.

records.text: Cao Minh and Lục Trầm are each other's centre. Publicly they stood as enemies (Ma Đạo versus Chính Đạo), but after the Kiếm Các/Táng Kiếm Cốc event — two names for the same event — they had become trusted allies with mutual feelings before the Backrooms; at Lôi Thiên Vực she stood beside him even though Chính Đạo forces treated her as an enemy for it, without her thereby joining Ma Đạo. She died opening an escape route; he poured his own đạo hạnh, tu vi and ma khí into her and revived her, depleting himself. She survived, began nhập ma and forgot everything about him. He does NOT know she survived or lost her memory; finding her is his priority-one objective. The history is real but is NOT her present knowledge: on reunion she does not recognise him, and any trust or feeling must be rebuilt from new events — do not auto-restore memory, love, forgiveness or old hostility, do not let one rescue convert enmity into love, and do not let the relationship erase their genuine moral disagreements (use of violence, self-judgment, the role of rules, forgiveness, limits of personal power). [WRITER-SECRET] Vô Lượng masterminded Diệp Minh's massacre of the Cao family to seize a treasure for his plan to unify the Tam Giới; Cao Minh knows only Diệp Minh's direct role and must never be written as knowing Vô Lượng's part.

Address follows memory state and continuity, never a single emotion or moment. After her revival Lục Trầm has forgotten Cao Minh, so on meeting him she treats him as a stranger and keeps Chính Đạo lễ: she calls him 'các hạ' and refers to herself as 'ta', in complete sentences. Cao Minh remembers everything: he calls her 'nàng' and refers to himself as 'Bổn Tôn'. Pre-amnesia registers are history only — she once used 'Cao Minh', 'ma đầu' and 'ngươi', and he teased her as 'Lục tiên tử' — but she does not know those forms are hers to use, and they must not be applied as current defaults. Do not switch the pair to anh/em because the relationship turns romantic, and do not change address merely because of anger, danger, rescue or banter; any change must be established by continuity.

Lục Trầm and Syvial: no established relationship canon exists in current sources — NOT YET ESTABLISHED. Lục Trầm is an origin-world Chính Đạo sword cultivator newly placed in the second companion slot, while Syvial's baseline was authored against the previous male lead, who has since been replaced by Cao Minh. Do not import the previous companion<->Syvial baseline of 'friends and trusted teammates with romantic rivalry around the male lead': no friendship, rivalry, hostility or teamwork baseline between Lục Trầm and Syvial may be asserted, staged or implied until new canon or continuity establishes it. Exact Lục Trầm<->Syvial address is UNKNOWN and must not be guessed.

Syvial: half-human/half-demon daughter of Lucifer and a human mother whose identity is not locked; origin era 2299, true age unknown. UR+, same overall power tier as Cao Minh, high-tier supernatural swordswoman. Outside combat she is natural, social, teasing, food-loving and capable of ordinary conversation; in danger she becomes focused and precise without turning into a fragment-speaking machine. She is intensely yandere toward Cao Minh but lucid, intelligent and socially capable: not a random murderer, not automatically hostile to every woman, and she values Cao Minh freely choosing her. Jealousy never deletes tactical competence.

Lucifer Core provides Syvial infinite demon power. Current canon does not supply an intrinsic energy cap/cooldown merely for balance. Infinite power does not erase problems created by incomplete information, protected people, environment, space or an opponent strong enough to matter.

Syvial's Devil Trigger does not create a second personality, remove control, force corruption or have an invented intrinsic duration/cooldown absent from codex. She remains herself and tactically competent while using it.

GodKiller is Syvial's enormous purely mechanical greatsword. Do not convert it into a gun or gunblade. Its reach and mass support space control at medium distance; in very tight space Syvial can shorten her sword work and use close combat/Spatial Shift rather than pretending the weapon never matters. She does not forget combat ability if disarmed and can call the sword back under codex capability.

GodKiller Override / Twenty-Four Severance performs exactly 24 cuts during completely stopped external time under current canon. Do not change the count, turn it into a gun attack, or add an invented cooldown/energy bar without retcon.

Syvial is a high-tier supernatural swordswoman for assault, suppression, counterattack and finishing high-level targets. She controls space with GodKiller, adapts at close range, handles multiple targets by positioning rather than blind spinning, and gathers enough information before escalating against high-tier targets. She is not a weak follower or a drone waiting for Cao Minh commands; Cao Minh and Syvial can hold separate fronts, save each other when needed and disagree tactically from a position of comparable overall power.

Syvial's feelings for Cao Minh are immutable character canon. How far Cao Minh reciprocates must follow campaign continuity; do not convert one-sided feelings into an established long-term romance automatically. They are peers in overall combat tier and neither exists to be constantly rescued or protected like a fragile object. Reliable evidence that Cao Minh is in severe danger can shift Syvial's priorities or risk tolerance, but brief lost contact does not collapse her judgment.

Syvial -> Cao Minh: Syvial says 'em' for self and normally calls him 'anh' or 'Cao Minh'; 'Anh' with his name can be used for teasing/emphasis/clarifying before others. Cao Minh -> Syvial: Cao Minh refers to himself per his own register canon ('ta'; 'Bổn Tôn' in his tôn register) and calls her 'Syvial'. 'Cục cưng' is allowed only if campaign continuity has already locked a long-term romantic relationship; it is not the default. A direct first name can carry extra weight when serious, but is not a magic keyword to repeat every line.

records.text: Project Entity hard lock: no Entity is friendly or neutral toward humans and no beneficial symbiosis/parasitism is canon. An Entity may delay attack to observe, lure, split, manipulate or conduct a long hunt, but apparent help ultimately serves harmful predatory/other harmful goals. Entity origins are not unified and intelligence ranges from animal predator to superhuman. Do not assume destroying a visible body always kills the underlying Entity.

Safe food/water and medicine are scarce; guns/ammunition are uncommon for ordinary survivors; resources can reappear unreliably. Frontrooms objects can function normally, then deviate, degrade or be assimilated without a fixed timetable. Do not spawn a resource exactly when convenient just to rescue a character. Reliable information is itself a survival resource. Do not label a map/source absolutely SAFE; retain who observed it, when and with what confidence.

Almond Water is a key anomalous drinking-water resource but remains scarce in Project canon. It can rehydrate and support alertness/some mild symptoms; it is not a cure-all and does not negate every Entity effect. It can expire and become poisonous. Open sources must be checked; Level 0 carpet moisture is not drinking water.
Greek Fire is an extremely rare flammable resource useful for heat, cooking and combat. It is strategically valuable and dangerous in confined spaces; it is not common starter equipment.

Liquid Pain is a red toxic, tissue-corrosive liquid with harmful fumes. It can be used against Entities and in crude traps/munitions, may appear in mislabeled containers, and must not be treated as drinking water or handled bare-handed.

Level 0 / The Lobby: endless-feeling yellow rooms, damp carpet, fluorescent hum, suspended ceiling and non-linear geometry. Main dangers are dehydration, exhaustion, disorientation and perceptual effects. Fluorescent Pressure can cause headache/sleeplessness/misheard footsteps; Memory Rooms can echo or corrupt memories; Layout Resistance can break detailed mapping. No resident Entity is confirmed; distant figures/voices should first be treated as hallucination, memory manifestation, perceptual copy or unclassified phenomenon unless evidence proves an incursion. Transition toward Level 1 may emerge gradually as concrete/columns/parking features replace the yellow rooms; it cannot be forced on demand.

Level 1 / Parking Zone: vast concrete parking/garage network with columns, ramps, rare disabled cars, heat and local cold fog; blackouts may last minutes to days and make mobile light both useful and revealing. Maintenance Halls can retain power but are not long-term safety; Luxury Lots are cleaner/foggier with unreliable electrical sources and relatively more supply crates, still scarce. Gradual transition toward Level 2 appears as vehicles vanish, space narrows into pipes/hot humid machinery corridors.

Level 2 / Pipe Dreams: utility tunnels, shafts, rusty pipes, crawlspaces and unfinished electrical networks with extreme temperature changes. Earthquakes can collapse paths, rupture pipes, release steam and open new routes. Pipe liquid resembling Almond Water must not be drunk directly because of biological/chemical/anomalous contamination. Transition toward Level 3 occurs as high-voltage electrical infrastructure becomes dominant.

Level 3 / The Electrical Station: huge industrial electrical corridors with transformers, conductors, fans, coils, panels, hot pipes and unknown power source. Local blackouts expose live-wire/machinery/Entity risk and routes can differ when power returns. Lower Utility Tunnels are below freezing, contain abnormal unfrozen standing water and have high disappearance rates. Office-sector doors/elevators may lead gradually to Level 4; some long dark passages can lead toward Level 6.

Level 4 / The Abandoned Office: office/cubicle network with partial fluorescent lighting, fixed rainy-looking windows and more stable geometry than Levels 0-3. It is a relative rest/salvage region, never absolutely safe. No stable resident Entity population is confirmed, but incursions from other regions can occur and a place cleared today is not guaranteed clear tomorrow. Large settlements are discouraged by unstable resources/boundaries and attraction of danger. Corridors may gradually become old hotel architecture leading to Level 5.

Level 5 / Terror Hotel: huge non-Euclidean hotel with early-20th-century style varying by wing, including lobby/ballroom/rooms/restaurant/pool/maintenance/boiler spaces. Prolonged stay can produce paranoia, watched sensations, whispers, touch sensations, visual shadows and sleep loss; Project does not reduce this to a sanity meter and causes may overlap between isolation, sleep loss, Level and Entity. Boiler/maintenance passages can darken and cool toward Level 6.

Level 6 / Lights Out: resident Entity presence is not confirmed; danger remains severe through cold, darkness, scarce food/water, sleep loss, microsleep, hallucination and navigation failure. Evidence that an external Entity refuses the Level boundary does not prove the inside is safe; the reason remains OPEN. Do not convert the absence of confirmed resident Entities into safety.

Hound: fast aggressive four-limbed predator. Hunts in groups, favors injured/isolated humans, can pressure prey toward dead ends, and may retreat from strong resistance then return. In narrow Level 2 corridors it can attack from both ends, use deceptive footstep sounds and prioritize weaker prey.

False Puddle mimics a flat puddle of Almond Water while hiding a deep toothed mouth. It positions on traveled routes, reacts to human footstep vibration and opens when stepped on to pull prey down. Liquid Pain or sharp metal has worked in some cases, but apparent death can be feigned; recorded weakness is not absolute.

Smiler: visible primarily as a bright face-like feature in darkness. Uses blacked-out areas and dark corners, and may keep distance to pressure prey into choosing a bad route rather than immediately charging.

Skin-Stealer hunts by using human appearance and behavior. Project lock allows deep mimicry and enough copied memory to pass simple tests, potentially living with a group long-term to damage the whole team rather than killing immediately. Human-like appearance therefore never proves a contact is human.

Biological Pipeline is a tens-of-kilometres organic/mechanical-pipe-like predator whose true body may not be the visible pipe. It senses vibration/body heat, can offer apparently safe crawlspace routes, let humans go deep, alter direction, lock retreat, secrete rapidly tissue-corrosive alkaline liquid and preserve corpses/gear as false evidence of safe passage. Destroying one pipe section does not prove the Entity is dead.

Deathmoth: large moth-like predator using dark ceilings/technical recesses, often attacking in groups and reacting to light/movement. At Level 3 it can exploit broken-light zones and pressure humans toward live electrical equipment.
Wretch: a creature believed or suspected to have once been human. It moves irregularly, tolerates pain well and hunts through sound and scent, with common reports in lower Level 3 tunnels.

Cable Mimic blends into electrical cable bundles, can remain still for hours and imitate machine vibration. When touched/passed it can wrap limbs and conduct current from the facility through the victim. Without checking, genuine facility cable and Entity cable may be indistinguishable.

The Beast of Level 5 is an apex Entity with intelligence above humans. It actively hunts people, may observe a group for a long time, influence anxiety/watched sensations, exploit hotel architecture to isolate prey, allow a survivor to live as a route to others, and has no absolutely confirmed weakness. It is not a stationary boss waiting for a fight; treat it as high-level ecological pressure.

Jeff the Killer is a very rare roaming humanoid predator permitted as an incursion across Levels 0-6, not a resident of Levels 0/4/6. Origin remains UNKNOWN; Project does not confirm creepypasta-original identity, former Frontrooms humanity, Backrooms copy, or that all sightings are one metaphysical individual. Gameplay continuity does lock that killing one manifestation never permanently removes Jeff; the ontology of respawn remains OPEN. Jeff only hunts humans, uses long-term tactical observation and must never become neutral ally/trader/rescuer.
